Options: A) Physical components of a computer that can be touched
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Hardware: all tangible, physical components — CPU, RAM, hard disk, keyboard, monitor, etc.

Options: A) Programs and instructions that tell hardware what to do
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Software: intangible programs and data — OS, applications, utilities, drivers.

Options: A) The brain of the computer that executes instructions
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: CPU: processes all instructions and calculations. Contains ALU (arithmetic), CU (control), and registers.

QuestionText: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) in the CPU
Options: A) Performs arithmetic and logical operations
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: ALU: the part of the CPU that carries out arithmetic (+,-,*,/) and logical (AND, OR, NOT, comparisons) operations.

QuestionText: The Control Unit (CU) in the CPU
Options: A) Directs the flow of instructions and coordinates all CPU components
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Control Unit: fetches instructions from memory, decodes them, and coordinates ALU, registers, and I/O to execute them.

Options: A) GHz (gigahertz) — clock cycles per second
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: CPU clock speed (GHz): the number of instruction cycles per second. Higher GHz = faster processing (other factors also matter).

Options: A) Data currently in use — volatile, loses data on power off
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: RAM: fast, volatile working memory for active programs and data. More RAM allows more programs to run simultaneously.

QuestionText: The storage capacity of RAM is measured in
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: RAM is measured in GB (4 GB, 8 GB, 16 GB). Larger RAM = more programs and data held in memory simultaneously.

Options: A) Permanent firmware (BIOS/UEFI) that doesn't change on power off
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: ROM: non-volatile memory with pre-programmed, unchangeable instructions needed at startup.

Options: A) Magnetic secondary storage with spinning platters for long-term data
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: HDD: uses magnetic coating on rotating disks; stores OS, apps, and files permanently. Slower than SSD.

Options: A) Flash memory-based secondary storage; faster and more durable than HDD
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: SSD: no moving parts; faster access, lower power, more durable than HDD; increasingly replacing HDDs.

QuestionText: Which storage device has the fastest data access speed?
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: SSD access times ~0.1 ms; HDD ~5-10 ms (moving parts). RAM is even faster but volatile.

Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Monitor (display): output device showing visual information.

Options: A) Input device (enters text and commands)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Keyboard: input device for entering text, numbers, and commands.

Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Mouse: pointing input device that controls cursor and selects items on screen.

Options: A) Output device (produces physical copies of documents)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Printer: output device that produces hard copies (paper output) of documents and images.

Options: A) Input device (converts physical documents to digital)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Scanner: input device that digitises physical documents, photos, and images.

Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Microphone: input device that captures sound waves and converts them to digital signals.

Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Speakers/headphones: output devices that convert digital audio signals to sound waves.

Options: A) Input device (captures video and images)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Webcam: input device that captures live video for video calls, streaming, or recording.

QuestionText: A touch screen is both an
Options: A) Input and output device (displays and detects touch input)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Touch screen: display (output) with a touch-sensitive layer (input) — combined I/O device.

Options: A) RAM and ROM — directly accessible by CPU
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Primary storage: directly accessible by CPU at high speed. Includes RAM (volatile) and ROM (non-volatile).

Options: A) HDD, SSD, USB drives, optical discs — stores data long-term
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Secondary storage: non-volatile, stores data permanently but accessed slower than primary. HDD, SSD, USB, DVD.

Options: A) Very fast memory built into the CPU to store frequently used data
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Cache (L1, L2, L3): extremely fast, small memory inside/near the CPU. Stores frequently accessed data to reduce CPU wait time.

QuestionText: The memory hierarchy from fastest to slowest is
Options: A) Registers > Cache > RAM > SSD > HDD
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Speed order (fastest→slowest): Registers > L1/L2/L3 Cache > RAM > SSD > HDD > Optical/Tape.

Options: A) Hard disk space as an extension of RAM when RAM is full
D) CPU registers as extra RAM
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Virtual memory: OS uses a page file/swap space on the disk to extend available memory when RAM is insufficient.

Options: A) The main circuit board connecting all computer components
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Motherboard (mainboard): the primary PCB connecting CPU, RAM, storage, expansion cards, and I/O ports.

QuestionText: The BIOS chip is located on
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System): firmware stored in ROM on the motherboard; initialises hardware at startup.

QuestionText: A GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is used for
Options: A) Processing and rendering graphics (images, video, 3D)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: GPU: specialised processor for rendering graphics. Modern GPUs also used for AI/ML and scientific computing.

Options: A) Universal Serial Bus (for connecting peripheral devices)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: USB: standard interface for connecting peripherals (keyboards, mice, storage, phones) to computers.

Options: A) Transmit high-definition video and audio between devices
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface): transmits uncompressed HD video and audio via a single cable.

QuestionText: The power supply unit (PSU) in a computer
Options: A) Converts AC mains power to DC voltages for computer components
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: PSU: converts 110-240V AC from the wall to stable DC voltages (5V, 12V, 3.3V) required by computer components.

QuestionText: Optical storage devices (CD, DVD, Blu-ray) use
Options: A) Laser light to read and write data
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Optical discs: laser beam reads/writes data encoded as microscopic pits and lands on a reflective surface.

QuestionText: A flash drive (USB pen drive) uses
Options: A) Flash memory (NAND) for portable storage
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: USB flash drive: portable, solid-state flash memory device. No moving parts; compact and rewritable.

Options: A) Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: SDRAM: synchronised to the CPU clock speed for faster data transfer than asynchronous DRAM.

Options: A) Devices are automatically recognised and configured when connected
C) Only works with specific OS
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Plug and play: OS automatically detects and configures newly connected devices without manual driver installation.

QuestionText: A barcode reader is an ___ device
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Barcode reader: input device that uses laser/LED to scan and decode barcode data.

Options: A) Fingerprint scanner, iris scanner, and facial recognition
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Biometric input: captures unique biological features (fingerprint, iris, face) for identification/authentication.

QuestionText: A light pen is an ___ device
Options: A) Input device (pointing directly at the screen)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Light pen: an input device used to point directly at screen positions; detects light from the screen's refresh.

QuestionText: The number of pixels displayed on screen is called
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Screen resolution: number of pixels horizontally × vertically. Higher resolution = sharper, more detailed image.

QuestionText: Refresh rate of a monitor is measured in
Options: A) Hz (hertz) — number of times screen refreshes per second
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Refresh rate (Hz): how many times per second the screen is redrawn. 60 Hz standard; 144 Hz+ for gaming.

Options: A) The resolution/precision of a printer or scanner
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: DPI: dots printed per inch. Higher DPI = sharper, more detailed print/scan output.

Options: A) Spraying tiny droplets of ink onto paper
B) Fusing toner powder with heat
C) Using laser and photoreceptor drum
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Inkjet: sprays microscopic ink droplets through tiny nozzles onto paper. Good for colour, photos.

Options: A) Using a laser beam, photoreceptor drum, and heat-fused toner
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Laser printer: laser draws image on charged drum; toner adheres to charged areas; heat fuses toner to paper.

Options: A) Bytes, KB, MB, GB, TB (in increasing order)
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Bytes → KB (1024 B) → MB (1024 KB) → GB (1024 MB) → TB (1024 GB) → PB.

Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: 1 GB = 1024 MB (binary). In marketing, 1 GB = 1000 MB is often used. In computing: 1 GiB = 1024 MiB.

QuestionText: Input devices feed data ___ the computer
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Input devices: keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone — they send data INTO the computer for processing.

QuestionText: Output devices send data ___ the computer
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Output devices: monitor, printer, speakers — they present processed information to the user.

QuestionText: A plotter is a specialised output device used for
Options: A) Printing large-scale technical drawings and blueprints
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Plotter: precision output device for large-format technical drawings (CAD diagrams, maps, engineering blueprints).

Options: A) Reduce strain and improve comfort during extended computer use
Topic: Computer - Hardware, Software, I/O Devices and Memory
Explanation: Ergonomic hardware (curved keyboards, vertical mice, adjustable monitors) reduces repetitive strain injury (RSI).
